clue.text: A pint drunk before a film

indicators.note: drunk suggests something reeling and jumbled, so the letters of the first two words are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone sinks a pint before settling down to watch a movie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'film' looks like a cinema trip after the drink, but it is the definition: a thin coating, not a movie.
explanation.definitionFit: A patina is a thin surface layer or coating, such as the green sheen on old bronze.

clue.text: Cut back all around plant

parts.note: to prune is to cut back a shrub or tree

indicators.note: around signals that the word all is turned round to read backwards

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A gardener trims back everything growing round a particular plant.
explanation.walkthrough: Prunella is the first name of the actor Prunella Scales, whose 90th birthday the puzzle marks; 2 and 3 together give her name.
explanation.definitionFit: Prunella is a genus of low-growing herbs, including selfheal.

clue.text: It's essential to calibrate this device

definitions.text: It's essential to calibrate this device

parts.words: It's essential to calibrate this device
parts.note: a weighing device must be calibrated to give true readings, and the clue describes it by that need

explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as general engineering advice; it describes a weighing machine. With 2 it gives the actor Prunella Scales.
explanation.definitionFit: A weighing machine must be set accurately against known weights to be trusted.

clue.text: The first sort of test in old solver's book

indicators.note: in places the first pieces inside the archaic possessive

parts.note: the solver is 'you', and the old form of 'your' is thy
as in Elizabeth the First, written Elizabeth I
the MOT is the annual roadworthiness test for British vehicles

explanation.surface: An old exam paper in a solver's book apparently starts with a particular kind of test.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The first' is I, the regnal numeral as in Elizabeth I. The MOT is Britain's yearly vehicle safety test. Timothy West, Prunella Scales's husband, is 4 and 11.
explanation.definitionFit: Timothy is one of the epistles in the New Testament of the Bible.

clue.text: Crazy cooking keeps duck cold

indicators.note: keeps means the mixed letters hold the next piece inside them
cooking stirs ingredients up, so the letters of crazy are mixed

parts.note: a duck in cricket is a score of zero, which looks like O

explanation.surface: Some wild kitchen method keeps a duck chilled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooking' turns CRAZY into CORYZA's outer letters, CRYZA, and 'keeps' puts O inside them.
explanation.definitionFit: Coryza is the medical term for the inflamed, runny nose of a common cold.

clue.text: Thrilled about muck-up? That's harsh!

indicators.note: about means the first word's synonym goes round the other piece

parts.note: to be sent is to be thrilled or carried away, as by music

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word is read bottom to top, so backwards

parts.note: muck is dirt

explanation.surface: Someone excited about a blunder is told that is a cruel reaction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'muck-up' reads as one word for a blunder, but it splits: 'muck' is the dirt and 'up', in a down clue, turns it backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A strident sound or tone is loud and grating, so harsh to the ear.

clue.text: Composition of the month? I see that's also going around in Colombia

indicators.note: in places the pieces inside the country code

parts.note: CO is the international code for Colombia
Apr is the calendar abbreviation for April
I plus C, which sounds like see

indicators.note: going around says the repeated pair is turned backwards

parts.note: the same pair as before, I and C, repeated

explanation.surface: Someone asks which piece of music is this month's, then notes it is also on tour in Colombia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's also' stands for a second copy of what 'I see' just gave, and 'going around' turns only that second copy.
explanation.definitionFit: A capriccio is a lively, free-form piece of music, so a musical work.

clue.text: Busybody shopper, as originally depicted on TV? Triumphantly, yes

indicators.note: originally points to the start of each word, so take their first letters

explanation.surface: A nosy shopper from television is asked about, and someone answers with a triumphant yes.
explanation.walkthrough: Prunella Scales played Dotty, a fussy, interfering shopper, in a long-running series of TV adverts for the British supermarket Tesco.
explanation.definitionFit: The character in the supermarket adverts was a meddling customer, always poking into others' shopping.

clue.text: Remarkable fight that's seen from passing train?

parts.note: signal as an adjective means notable or striking
to box is to fight with fists

explanation.surface: A dramatic brawl is witnessed by passengers on a passing train.
explanation.definitionFit: The trackside cabin from which railway signals are operated is glimpsed by passengers going by.

clue.text: Somewhat brassy, bilious hotelier's wife

indicators.note: Somewhat says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A description of a woman who is rather loud and bad-tempered, married to a hotel owner.
explanation.walkthrough: Sybil Fawlty, wife of hotelier Basil in the BBC sitcom Fawlty Towers, was Prunella Scales's most famous role.
explanation.definitionFit: In the sitcom Fawlty Towers, Sybil is married to Basil, who runs the Torquay hotel.

clue.text: Point of view established

indicators.note: of here means the answer is made of letters taken from the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of view into established

explanation.surface: Someone's opinion has become settled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Point of view' reads as one phrase, but 'Point' is the definition and the answer hides in 'view established'. Timothy West is the actor married to Prunella Scales.
explanation.definitionFit: West is one of the four cardinal points of the compass.

clue.text: Bit of a thick skin that's required to contact the Guardian?

parts.note: to call someone is to contact them by phone
the clue appears in the Guardian, so the paper speaking of itself is us

explanation.surface: The newspaper suggests it takes some nerve to get in touch with its staff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'thick skin' suggests needing courage to phone the paper; read literally it is a patch of hardened skin.
explanation.definitionFit: A callus is a hardened, thickened patch of skin formed by repeated rubbing.

clue.text: Reportedly, the male host behaved like an ass

indicators.note: Reportedly says the words are to be heard rather than spelt

parts.note: he is a male, and a host is a horde, a great crowd

explanation.surface: Word has it that the man throwing the party acted the fool.
explanation.walkthrough: In British speech, which drops the R, 'he horde' sounds just like 'hee-hawed'. 'ass' is taken literally: a donkey.
explanation.definitionFit: A donkey's bray is written hee-haw, so making that call is acting like one.

clue.text: Flyer heralding a lovely short film

indicators.note: heralding means coming ahead of, so the bird goes first

parts.note: a tit is a small bird, so a flyer

indicators.note: short means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: nice means lovely

explanation.surface: A leaflet announcing a charming brief movie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flyer' looks like a printed leaflet; it is a bird. 'short' cuts NICE to NIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Titanic is James Cameron's 1997 blockbuster about the doomed ocean liner.

clue.text: Hero worship? Puck does have a go, after taking note

indicators.note: after places the attempt following the note

parts.note: Puck is the setter, who would say 'I do'
la is the sixth note of the sol-fa scale
to try is to have a go

explanation.surface: The setter admits to having a shot at idolising someone, once a note has been taken.
explanation.walkthrough: Setters refer to themselves by their pseudonym, so 'Puck does' is I DO.
explanation.definitionFit: Idolatry is excessive adoration, like worshipping a hero as an idol.

clue.text: Article describing 2 3 and 4 11

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a single thing or entry, such as an article in a list
second meaning: a romantic couple, as Prunella Scales and Timothy West are

explanation.walkthrough: The cross-references give the married actors Prunella Scales and Timothy West; a couple is called an item.
explanation.definitionFit: An item is an individual thing, and informally a pair in a romantic relationship.

clue.text: State in which there's no point heading off for public service

indicators.note: heading off says the front letter is removed

parts.words: State in which there's no point
parts.note: futility is the state of being pointless

explanation.surface: A cynic calls public service a pointless business, with no point heading off anywhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading off' removes the F from FUTILITY.
explanation.definitionFit: A utility is a company supplying an essential service such as water, gas or electricity.

clue.text: Discovering inclination is about right

indicators.note: is about means the synonym goes round the next piece

parts.note: a leaning is an inclination or tendency

explanation.surface: A tendency to lean towards what is correct.
explanation.definitionFit: Learning is finding out, as in learning the news, so discovering.

clue.text: Support husband or wife online?

parts.note: E stands for electronic, as in email
a spouse is a husband or wife

explanation.surface: A quip about whether a married partner met online is an e-spouse.
explanation.definitionFit: To espouse a cause is to adopt and support it.

clue.text: Nice days, clinching return of desire for outings

indicators.note: clinching means holding tight, so the French word holds the reversed piece

parts.note: Nice is a French city, and French for days is jours

indicators.note: return of says the following word is turned backwards

parts.note: a yen is a longing or desire

explanation.surface: Pleasant days that settle the comeback of a longing for trips out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nice' looks like the adjective but is the French city, so its days are JOURS. 'return of' turns YEN to NEY.
explanation.definitionFit: Journeys are trips from one place to another, so excursions.

clue.text: Sounds like fantastic gun for acting president

indicators.note: Sounds like says the answer is heard as the words that follow

parts.note: a ray gun is the weapon of science fantasy

explanation.surface: Someone recommends a sci-fi weapon for a stand-in head of state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'acting president' looks like a temporary leader, but it means a president who acted.
explanation.definitionFit: Ronald Reagan was a Hollywood film actor before becoming US president.

clue.text: Charmingly old-fashioned designer carries one

indicators.note: carries means the designer holds the next piece within

parts.note: Mary Quant was the British fashion designer famed for the miniskirt
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A designer with a quaint touch carries one item.
explanation.walkthrough: Mary Quant was the 1960s London fashion designer.
explanation.definitionFit: Quaint describes something attractively unusual in an old-fashioned way.

clue.text: Residents in very louvred part of New York

definitions.meaning: first meaning: ..., as royal residents of palaces such as the Louvre in Paris
second meaning: one of New York City's five boroughs

explanation.walkthrough: The Louvre was a royal palace before it became a museum, so its residents included queens. Prunella Scales also played the Queen on screen.
explanation.definitionFit: Queens is a borough of New York City, and queens are royal consorts or monarchs living in palaces.

clue.text: Number that's in excess

parts.note: in Roman numerals this number is written XC, and those letters sit inside the word excess

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a surplus amount; the Roman numeral for this number, XC, appears in eXCess. It is also the birthday being marked.
explanation.definitionFit: Ninety is nine tens, written XC in Roman numerals.

clue.text: Writer leaves maneater in locked passage

indicators.note: leaves means the writing piece departs from the longer word

parts.note: a cannibal eats human flesh
a nib is the point of a pen, the part that writes

explanation.surface: An author escapes a man-eating creature trapped in a sealed corridor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Writer' looks like an author; it is the pen nib.
explanation.definitionFit: A canal is a waterway with locks that let boats move between levels.

clue.text: The rarest eagle? Of course it is!

definitions.text: The rarest eagle? Of course it is!

parts.words: The rarest eagle? Of course it is!
parts.note: in golf an eagle is two under par, and on a par three the only way to get one is a single stroke, a rare feat on the course

explanation.walkthrough: 'eagle' suggests the bird, and 'Of course' an exclamation; both are golf, an eagle being two under par and the course being the links.
explanation.definitionFit: Getting the ball in with one stroke on a par-three hole scores two under par, the rarest kind of eagle.

clue.text: Big jar, say

indicators.note: say signals that the word is spoken aloud, giving a sound-alike

parts.note: to grate is to jar, to have a harsh, irritating effect

explanation.surface: A large pot, for instance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jar' looks like a pot, but it is the verb meaning to grate.
explanation.definitionFit: Great means large in size or amount.

clue.text: What Salem's Lot horrifically has — the ultimate in scary foolishness

parts.note: the town in Stephen King's horror novel has evil, so it has a sin in it

indicators.note: the ultimate in means the last letter of the next word

parts.note: its last letter is Y

explanation.surface: A comment on a horror novel's town and its foolish scares.
explanation.walkthrough: Salem's Lot is Stephen King's vampire novel; the town 'has a sin in it', horrifically. Add the last letter of 'scary'.
explanation.definitionFit: Asininity is the quality of being asinine, utterly stupid.
